title: Host capability manifest
description: What one host can actually express in an agent definition file, and how. The renderer consults this instead of assuming; anything a host cannot express becomes a disclosure in the generated file rather than a silently dropped guarantee. Every 'supported: false' must carry a 'verified' note, so a capability is never absent merely because nobody checked.

verified_on.description: The date this manifest was last checked against the host's own documentation or binary. Stale capability claims are how the previous revision came to assert that reasoning effort was unsettable on a host that had supported it for two releases.

source.description: Where verified_on's check was made: a documentation URL, or a command whose output was read.

agent_dir.description: Where these agent files belong in a project that consumes this plugin, in that host's own convention.

bundled_dir.description: Where the renderer writes this host's generated agents, relative to the repository root. Since ADR 0001 step 4 that is adapters/<host>/agents/ for every host, which is decision 3 of that ADR: generated agents live in the adapter tree, and the build places them wherever the host wants them. It cannot be dist/<host>/ any more - build_adapter empties that directory before writing it, so a renderer aiming there would be building the input to its own erasure.

root_placeholder.description: How a generated agent file on this host refers to the plugin root. Claude Code expands ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; hosts with no such variable get a literal placeholder root resolves in the brief. Defaults to <skill_root> when absent.

tool_map.description: Portable tool intent -> the host's own tool names. An intent absent from this map cannot be expressed on this host.

enforced_prohibitions.description: Portable must_not ids this host makes structurally impossible, whatever a role declares - a tool the host strips from every agent, for example. Optional; absent means nothing beyond what the capabilities already imply. Prohibitions the renderer can DERIVE from tool_map plus the role's own grant are deliberately not listed here: a derived claim changes when the grant changes, a declared one can drift away from the truth.

model_map.description: Vendor-neutral tier -> this host's model id. Never 'inherit'.

effort_map.description: Portable effort level -> how this host spells it. Null when capabilities.reasoning_effort.supported is false.

read_only_enforced.description: True only where the host itself refuses writes. Omitting write tools from an allowlist counts; an instruction telling the agent not to write does not, and must be declared unsupported so the disclosure says so.

scoped_hooks.description: Whether the host can attach hooks to one agent definition rather than the whole session. Where false, prohibitions fall back to session-wide hooks keyed on the agent identity the host reports.

main_thread.description: What this host can express about an agent launched AS the main thread rather than dispatched into one. Optional, and optional on purpose: only root runs this way, so a host that ships no root needs to answer nothing here. A host that omits a sub-block declares nothing about it, and the renderer discloses the capability as absent rather than assuming either way.

verified.description: How this block was checked, as a whole.

delegate_scope.description: Whether this host can say WHICH agent types a delegating agent may spawn, and how it is spelled.

template.description: How the scoped grant is written, with {tool} and {types} substituted - `Agent({types})` on Claude Code. Required when supported is true. A template rather than a flag because the renderer must emit the host's own syntax, and hardcoding one host's spelling in the renderer is what this field undoes.

type_template.description: How an agent id becomes the type name this host matches, with {plugin} and {id} substituted. Separate from `template` because getting it wrong fails differently: a wrong wrapper is a syntax error, a wrong type name silently matches no agent and root can dispatch nothing.

separator.description: How multiple types are joined inside the template.

main_thread_only.description: True when the restriction binds only for an agent running as the main thread and is ignored in a dispatched agent's definition. This is the asymmetry root's isolation rests on: the same syntax is a guarantee for root and a decoration for the orchestrator, so the renderer must state enforcement differently for each. Absent means it binds wherever it is written.

initial_prompt.description: Whether this host auto-submits a prompt when a main-thread agent starts. Root's startup check depends on it: a check the agent must remember to run is a check that does not run on the session where it matters.

field.description: The literal key. Required when supported is true.
The literal key the renderer writes for this capability. Required when supported is true.

verified.description: How this was checked. For an unsupported capability this is the evidence of absence, not an assumption.

How this was checked. A prohibition belongs here only where the host makes it impossible to violate independently of the role's tool grant, so that the generated file can state enforcement rather than understate it.
